DeepSeek Harness: /btw asks the session's own model an aside without interrupting the running turn.
# dsh-btw
Side questions for DeepSeek Harness. `/btw <question>` asks the session's own model an aside while t
he main task keeps running: nothing is queued, the running turn is not interrupted, and the answer n
ever enters the model's conversation.
The command surface follows Grok Build's `/btw` (`crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/src/slash/commands/b
tw.rs` and `scrollback/blocks/btw.rs`): a command that bypasses the prompt queue, a golden-accented
`/btw <question>` row, and an answer kept outside the main turn. One deliberate difference: Grok ans
wers from the live session, while this plugin defaults to a standalone question with no conversation
at all; set `context: session` for the Grok behavior.
## Use
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- The row appears immediately with the question and `Answering…`, then shows the answer. The compose

r clears as soon as the command is admitted, not when the model replies.
- The answer is written by
the session's current provider and model. By default the question is standalone (`context: none`); `

context: session` also sends the conversation.
- Answers render Markdown: headings, lists, quotes, t

ables, fenced code, inline code, bold, italic, links.
- When the model reasons before answering, the
row carries a collapsible **Thinking** block above the answer, so the aside shows the work it did a

t the inherited thinking level.
- The summary line is a disclosure control like the host's own Turn
row: the question ellipsizes to one line, the chevron flips, and a click anywhere on the line folds

the answer away or brings it back. Fenced code keeps its line breaks in its own block.
- `Esc`, draf
ting, and the queue are untouched: a second question, a follow-up prompt, or a running turn all cont
are untouched: a second question, a follow-up prompt, or a running turn all continue independently.
The answer is not a model message and is not part of the next request. It is recorded as the command
lifecycle (`command/run`, `command/done`) in the session log, so it survives reload, fork, and repl
ay, and appears in the session transcript exactly once.
## Install
From a DeepSeek Harness profile, either form works — the published spec, or a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle inserts one Host row named `dsh-btw` and declares its browser half through `dsh.client`.
Enabling the row makes `/btw` available in the composer's command menu and registers the `/btw` rend
erer in the conversation.
### Configuration
Every key has a code default; the values in `cordis.patch.yml` are those defaults.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Mount the command at all. |
| `context` | `none` | What the side request may
see. `none` asks a standalone question with no conversation at all; `session` prepends the bounded c

onversation transcript below, which is what Grok's `/btw` does. |
| `description` | `旁问：不打断当前任务地提问 ·
Ask a side question without interrupting` | Copy shown under the composer's `/` list. The client re
nders a third-party Host command's catalog description verbatim, so this is the only place to set it

s wording and language. |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
- **Host** (`index.js`, `lib/`): registers the `btw` command with `ctx.commands.register()`. The sid
e request runs the session's own route — its provider, model, and reasoning effort — so an aside ans
wers at the same thinking level as the main turn, falling back to the profile default model's level
when the session never picked one. The handler runs outside any turn and returns at once: the compos
er keeps a claimed command's line until its handler returns, so awaiting the model there would hold
the user's draft for the whole request. `lib/answer-runner.js` then resolves the route from the sess
ion's current model selection (falling back to `session.requestHeader()`, then `ctx.agentDefaultMode
l`), streams one `ctx.llm.stream()` request with a fixed side-question policy and no tools, and sett
les the same row by appending `command/done` for the run's `commandId`. Under `context: session` it
first flattens `session.deriveMessages()` into a text-only transcript; under the default `none` the
request is the question alone. `llm` and `commands` are hard injections, so the plugin stays inactiv

e in a profile without them.
- **Client** (`client.js`): registers `conversation.chat.commandview` u
nder the key `btw`, the keyed slot the Chat view dispatches by command name. The component renders t
he question on the disclosure line and the answer as Markdown through a small block/inline parser th
is bundle owns (the host's Markdown component is not importable from a plugin); theming uses only `-
-dsw-alias-*` tokens, and text comes from the plugin's own locale namespace.
## Limitations
- `/btw` must start the message. Grok also hoists a mid-message `/btw` and treats the rest of the li
ne as the side question; the Harness command plane only resolves a command at byte zero, so `fix the

retry loop. /btw why?` is sent as an ordinary prompt.
- The answer arrives in one piece. The comman

d plane settles a handler once, so the row cannot stream tokens.
- Delivery is a second `command/don
e` for the originating `commandId` (the executor already logged one when the handler returned). The
Chat command node folds it into the existing row; readers that expect exactly one `command/done` per

run will see two.
- The lifecycle carries one `text` string, so a row with reasoning stores it inli
ne between `<<<btw:reasoning>>>` and `<<<btw:answer>>>` marker lines (`lib/result-text.js`). The row
parser reads them; the shipped generic command card, which does not, would show the markers as text

.
- Tool use, images, and plan-mode side requests are out of scope: the side request declares no too

ls and sends text only.
- A side question started from a session that has never sent a request needs

`provider` and `model` in the config, because there is no route to inherit yet.
- The `/` list draw
s a glyph and a localized title only for the six first-party definition ids in `dsh-client-ui-comman
ds`' `HOST_FACES` table; any other Host command renders its name plus this plugin's `description`. A
third-party command cannot add an icon there, and a client-side command contribution — which could
— takes no arguments, so `/btw <question>` would stop working.
